memory_update.text: VECO should be tracked as a second-order AI optical-interconnect equipment candidate because it disclosed $250M+ of InP laser-manufacturing equipment orders tied to 800G/1.6T hyperscale transceiver suppliers.

AXTI should be tracked as an upstream InP substrate candidate, but survival to later Serenity layers requires direct evidence of durable AI optical customer demand, export-permit stability, and capacity execution.

VIAV should be tracked as a testing/certification-gate candidate for 800G/1.6T AI fabrics, with key risk that AI optical validation may remain too small relative to broader telecom/network-test cyclicality.

Several optics names once fitting the $500M-$10B underfollowed lane have already repriced above the preferred band by 2026-06-11, so future passes should emphasize revenue mix, customer concentration, and unpriced bottleneck evidence rather than ticker novelty.

For AI networking and optical interconnect, the next chokepoint branches to test equipment, InP substrates, InP laser manufacturing tools, laser/TIA/driver components, module assembly, and optical DSP/NIC/switch silicon.

node: AI networking, optical interconnect, and high-speed data movement
summary: Layer 1B expanded the universe around AI optical networking away from obvious Ethernet leaders. Reference anchors such as Broadcom validate the 800G/1.6T optical DSP, NIC, and switch-silicon demand chain, but the underfollowed discovery lane points to less obvious bottleneck assets: InP laser manufacturing equipment, InP substrate supply, and optical/network test-validation gates. Current market-cap checks on 2026-06-11 show that several former small/mid-cap optics beneficiaries have already repriced above the preferred $500M-$10B hunting band, so this pass labels market-cap drift explicitly and prioritizes evidence-to-verify over conclusions.
